**Clarification on the bug report:** Sorry for the confusion in my initial description. Let me clarify the actual issue: **The root cause is NOT about which tools are being sent.** The model may refuse for any reason - safety filter, content policy, model limitations, etc. Thats expected behavior from the model. **The actual bugs are:** 1. **OpenCode doesnt display the refusal message** - The response clearly contains `"content":[{"type":"refusal","refusal":"Im sorry, but I cant help with that request."}]` but OpenCode shows nothing to the user. The conversation just empties silently. 2. **OpenCode wipes the conversation history** - When a refusal occurs, all previous messages disappear and `/revert` cannot restore them.

### Environment
- **OS**: macOS 26.6 (25G72)
- **OpenCode**: 1.18.23 (Desktop)
- **IME**: macOS built-in Simplified Chinese Pinyin
- **Browser**: Safari (Chrome confirmed unaffected)

### Reproduction Steps (100% reproducible)
1. Open a **new session** in the v2 prompt input.
2. Type any characters using the IME (e.g. `nihao`).
3. Press `Ctrl+A` to select all, then `Delete` to clear the input.
4. Start typing again with the IME.

**Expected**: The first keystroke enters the composition and joins the pinyin.

**Actual**: The first character is committed as literal text immediately; the remaining keystrokes stay in the IME candidate window, splitting the pinyin.

### Additional Findings
- **Japanese IME** shows the exact same behavior.
- The bug **does not occur** in an existing session that has already completed at least one round of prompt/response — only in a brand-new session.
- **Workaround**: After the second `Ctrl+A`, an invisible/transparent character remains in the input box. Deleting it (or pressing `Delete` once) restores normal IME composition.

### Screen Recording

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/390e82bc-4a97-49a0-9475-d83d74c0f449

### Environment
- **OS**: macOS 26.6 (25G72)
- **OpenCode Web**: served by OpenCode server 1.18.23
- **Browser**: Safari
- **IME**: macOS built-in Simplified Chinese Pinyin

### Reproduction
1. Open a new browser tab pointing to the OpenCode web app.
2. Focus the v2 prompt input and enable the Chinese IME.
3. Start typing continuously.

**Expected**: Pinyin composes normally and can be confirmed.

**Actual**: All letters except the last one are committed as plain English characters immediately; only the final keystroke remains in the composition. Chrome on the same machine does not exhibit this.

That lines up exactly with when this started breaking for people on my team — v1.18.4 was the last version that worked reliably, and every release from 1.18.5 through 1.18.22+ reproduces the issue.

I also wanted to share some data on the fix itself. **Update — local logs confirm a hard server-side `500`, not a client/network/geo issue**

Dug into `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` after our hangs:

```
level=ERROR message="stream error" providerID=opencode-go modelID=muse-spark-1.2-contributor
error.error="AI_APICallError: Internal server error"
```

Forensics from the log (opencode 1.18.13, macOS arm64):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total muse-spark-1.2-contributor events | 431 |
| Explicit `Internal server error` (500) entries | **41**, spanning 2026-08-23T17:40Z → 2026-08-25T18:14Z |
| Time from request start → error surfacing | **avg 0.61s** (min 0.42s, max 1.32s) across all 41 |
| Title agent (`small=true`) | fails with `AI_RetryError: Failed after 3 attempts` |
| Control: `deepseek-v4-flash`, same gateway, same machine, same window | 23 events, all succeed (~5s round trips) |

Two takeaways:

1. **The request reaches your gateway fine and gets rejected immediately with a 500** — sub-second RTT rules out regional blocking, IPv6 blackholes, or slow upstream. What looked like an infinite silent hang from the outside is just the CLI's internal retry loop hammering a model whose serving backend returns `500` every time.
2. Failure window started around **Aug 23 ~17:40 UTC**, which matches when other users would have started noticing — might help correlate with any deploy around that time.

Same model name served through a non-gateway provider (commandcode.ai, `meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor`) responds normally, so the model weights/serving stack per se work elsewhere.

Thanks for the pointers — we reviewed #42909, #15059, #34321, and #34243 (plus the related PRs).

**Same root cause.** Agreed: OpenCode can emit multiple `role: "system"` fragments / messages, and stock Qwen chat templates reject anything that is not a single system at `messages[0]`. Our failure mode matches those reports.

**Why we still filed this.** Distinct surface, not a different bug:
- Backend: **SGLang** on **DGX Spark** (`lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38-27b`, RadixArk NVFP4) — same OpenCode config worked under **vLLM**, broke after the engine/template switch.
- Repro includes **mid-conversation** systems (e.g. after tool rounds: `system → … → tool → system → user`), not only two adjacent systems at the head.
- We shipped a **working OpenCode plugin** (dual hook) rather than an external HTTP proxy.

**Assessment of existing proposals (for maintainers / other agents):**

| Approach | Status | vs our failure |
|---|---|---|
| Off-by-one `system.length > 2` → `> 1` (#34243 / #34321) | Correct but **narrow** | Fixes plugin `.push()` doubling the `system[]` array. Does **not** cover systems already inside the message history. |
| [#42801](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/42801) coalesce for `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` | Best narrow core PR we see; still open | Joins `system[]` before prepend. Good for head-of-request fragments. Still incomplete if a later `system` appears in `input.messages`. |
| [#16981](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/16981) / [#23501](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/23501) `systemMessage: "single" \| "multiple"` | Closest to a proper fix; still open | Capability-based merge at convert/dispatch is what we want upstream. |
| HTTP merge proxy (#42909) | Works | Same wire effect as our plugin; plugin keeps the fix inside OpenCode. |
| Custom / Unsloth chat template on the server | Works | Valid server-side escape hatch; we deliberately stay on the stock HF template from the MiaAI SGLang recipe. |

**Our workaround (confirmed on 1.18.23 + this SGLang stack):** coalesce via **both**
1. `experimental.chat.system.transform` — merge `output.system[]` → one fragment  
2. `experimental.chat.messages.transform` — merge all `system`/`developer` in the message list → one at index `0`

In-place mutate only (reassigning `output.system` / `output.messages` is a no-op). Sketch is in the issue body. Optional model flag `systemMessage: "single"` documents intent until core lands.

**Ask.** Please treat this as confirming evidence + a dual-hook reference implementation, not as a competing root cause. Happy to re-test nightlies once #42801 and/or #16981/#23501 land — and to report if mid-history systems still slip through after a head-only coalesce.

We will drop the plugin when upstream merge is stable.

Still reproducing on **v1.18.23** (win32 x64, Electron 42.3.3, Chrome 148.0.7778.218, Node 24.15.0) — adding quantified data from a debug bundle covering ~2 days of desktop usage on Windows.

Bursts sustain ~10 errors/second for minutes at a time (e.g. session 20260825T085543, `19:21:19`–`19:21:21` local), which matches the completely frozen UI described above.

### Escalation into a launch crash loop

Later the same day the problem escalated: six consecutive launches between 18:11 and 18:27 produced **no `renderer.log` at all** (renderer never got far enough to log anything), and Crashpad wrote two minidumps 2 seconds apart at the end of the sequence (`18:27:24`, 34 MB main-process dump, and `18:27:26`, 0.9 MB). Force-quit + relaunch remained the only recovery, consistent with the original report.

Side observation (probably environmental): during those launches the auto-updater failed with `net::ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT` after ~21 s each time.

I have the full debug bundle (text logs scanned clean of secrets) and both minidumps available if maintainers want them attached or uploaded elsewhere.

Ironically, I run opencode TUI all the time locally on this CachyOS laptop.

UPDATE: it is not strictly necessary to kill -9 the opencode. If I let it sit there long enough, it will exit on its own, but the mouse events "typing" issue still occurs.

There is no server.port nor server.hostname in my config file on the server.

Also, it does seem that new SSH attempts into the server are mostly blocked 99% of the time. Sometimes it gets through. I have to Stop the server in EC2 and Start it back up to get back normal function the fastest (or wait for opencode to eventually Exit on its own, which takes a really long time).

This issue might be a duplicate of or closely related to existing issues. Please check:

- #39738: Global config silently ignored when `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` is a symlink (stow/dotfile managers broken) — same root cause of symlink-unsafe writes, also affects GNU Stow users, though that issue reports the config being ignored rather than the symlink being replaced
- #36367: Credential writers follow existing symlinks for `auth.json` / JSON stores — related issue about symlink-following behavior in JSON write paths

If your issue is distinct (symlink replacement on `cli.json` preference save, vs. config being silently ignored), it may still be worth cross-referencing these for a unified fix.

Additional reproduction: this also affects the built-in `explore` subagent, documented as read-only.

With a global `permission: "allow"`, `opencode debug agent explore` showed effective permission entries that allowed `apply_patch`, `question`, `task`, and `skill`. An `explore` child session was then able to edit files, ask a user-facing approval question, and continue implementation work after a context compaction.

This is not only a Plan-mode UX concern: a global wildcard can silently remove the execution boundary of a specialized read-only subagent. A startup warning should cover every built-in agent whose documented safe behavior conflicts with its resolved effective permissions, and `debug agent` should make the overriding rule easy to identify.

following up on my own report, a couple of things in it might be wrong.

reinstalling same version stores once, the 266gb came from 516 distinct versions installed between 2026-06-10 and 2026-08-25 and never pruned. i think it was two and a half months not three weeks.

one version, 0.0.0-next-17444, was installed 200 times back to back over 33 hours. so that's the one costs cpu, bandwith and global npm install repeatedly overwriting the same thing which is #41495

on the cache side, the fix already exists in the same function. the bun branch of upgrade() installs into a scoped temp cache dir with a comment saying bun does not prune its shared cache. npm, pnpm and yarn just call the normal global install and inherit the user cache. npm takes --cache the same way.

For now, update to the latest beta, restart the background service, and clear npm's accumulated cache:

```bash
npm install -g @opencode-ai/cli@beta
opencode2 service restart
npm cache clean --force
```

Restarting the service is important: updating the package alone leaves the existing process running with its old in-memory version.
